item.title: Hugo Markdown Styling & Formatting Guide
item.dc:creator: Blanket Statement Team
item.description: A comprehensive showcase of typography, code highlighting, tables, quotes, and media formatting available in this Hugo blog starter.
item.content:encoded:
This starter template includes rich formatting support for technical writing, tutorial posts, and personal blogging. Below is a preview of the typography and components.

Headings & Typography

Here is standard body text with bold text, italic text, and inline code.

Subheading Level 3

Paragraph text flows smoothly with readable line heights and carefully tuned margins matching the Blanket Statement visual identity.

Subheading Level 4

Lists are formatted with clean spacing:

  • First bullet point with helpful context
  • Second bullet point with a link to home
  • Third bullet point with embedded sub-items:
    • Sub-item A
    • Sub-item B

Blockquotes

“Productive fidgeting transforms passive listening into active, engaged presence while building something beautiful for others.”

Code Syntax Highlighting

Hugo’s built-in Chroma syntax engine formats code with high contrast:

def knit_square(stitches=30, rows=48):
    """Simulate knitting a 7x9 inch square."""
    fabric = []
    for r in range(rows):
        fabric.append(["knit" for _ in range(stitches)])
    print(f"Finished square with {rows} rows of {stitches} stitches!")
    return fabric

if __name__ == "__main__":
    knit_square()

And in Go / Hugo template syntax:

{{ range where .Site.RegularPages "Section" "posts" }}
  <article>
    <h2>{{ .Title }}</h2>
    <p>{{ .Summary }}</p>
  </article>
{{ end }}

Tables

Block Length 9 inches Direction doesn’t matter
Yarn Weight Worsted (#4) Washable acrylic or wool blend
Needle Size US 8 (5.0mm) Provides flexible drape

Image Embeds

Images are automatically responsive with rounded corners and subtle shadows:

Enjoy writing your posts with Hugo!

item.title: A Beginner's Guide to Knitting 7” x 9” Squares
item.dc:creator: Devorah
item.description: Everything you need to know about casting on, garter stitch, gauge, and completing your first blanket block.
item.content:encoded:
Never held a pair of knitting needles before? No problem! Knitting a 7” x 9” blanket block is the single best starter project. There are no complicated increases or decreases—just a straightforward rectangle worked in classic Garter Stitch.

Materials Needed

  • Yarn: 1 skein worsted weight (medium #4) acrylic or washable wool.
  • Needles: US Size 8 (5.0 mm) or Size 9 (5.5 mm).
  • Ruler: The ruler printed on the ball band, or any standard measuring tape.
  • Tapestry Needle: To weave in your yarn ends.

Step-by-Step Instructions

Step 1: Cast On

Cast on approximately 28 to 34 stitches (depending on your needle size and yarn tension).

[ Needle ] ===o===o===o===o===o===o===o=== [ Cast on 30 sts ]

Tip: Measure your cast-on row against the ball band ruler. If it is 7 inches wide, you are ready to knit!

Step 2: The Garter Stitch

Every single row is worked in the knit stitch:

  1. Insert right needle into the front of the first stitch from left to right.
  2. Wrap working yarn counter-clockwise around the right needle.
  3. Pull the new loop through and slide the old stitch off the left needle.
  4. Repeat across the row!

Step 3: Knit Until 9 Inches

Continue knitting every row until the piece measures 9 inches from your cast-on edge. (Note: 9” x 7” is also fine—direction doesn’t matter!)

Step 4: Bind Off

  1. Knit two stitches.
  2. Use the left needle to lift the first stitch over the second stitch and off the needle.
  3. Knit the next stitch and repeat until one loop remains.
  4. Cut the yarn leaving a 6-inch tail, pull through the loop, and tighten.
